correctness.rationale: After translation to fix zero, quandle preservation implies f(-x)=-f(x), f(2y)=2f(y), and f(x+2y)=f(x)+f(2y). In particular the restriction to 2G is an additive bijection. A choice of its value on each representative then gives exactly the stated normal form. Conversely, 2a_c=g(2r_c) gives both the negation and translation identities, and distinct output cosets give bijectivity. Modulo 4G the doubling condition is theta(sigma(c))=g_bar(theta(c)). A compatible sigma fixing zero has (h-1)!(h!)^(k-1) choices by the fibers; any indicated output coset has exactly |(2G)[2]|=k lifts of the doubling condition, with the zero representative forced. This yields k^(hk-1), then the independent output translations and Aut(2G) give the formula. When k=1 it reduces to |G||Aut(2G)|(h-1)!; if also h=1 it gives the odd-group holomorph order. In the exponent-two case the operation is trivial and the formula gives |G|!, including the trivial group. The cyclic examples agree. The standard primary Aut count is the invertible-endomorphism proportion by equal-length cyclic blocks.
residual_risks: The finite examples are corroboration only. The test script's identification of C2 factors uses its chosen input conventions; it is not a general decomposition routine for mixed cyclic moduli. The written proof uses elementary divisors and does not have that dependency.

value.rationale: The all-groups classification and the even-factor fiber mechanism are useful in their own right. As a separate frozen contribution, however, the result repeats both the earlier exact invariant and its explicit map-level classification; the new notation is elementary decomposition of data in that prior formula. The few examples are routine substitutions, and the frozen scope adds no new abstract group structure, rigidity theorem or application beyond the covering record.
residual_risks: The rejection is of a separate scientific contribution, not of the utility or correctness of the already available formula.
